extra.message: LDAP injection (CWE-90): searchStaffByEmail() builds an LDAP search filter by concatenating the caller-supplied searchTerm directly: `(mail=${searchTerm})`. Unlike verifyGroupAccess() (which uses escapeLdapFilterValue), no escaping is applied. searchStaffByEmail is reachable from clients.new.tsx intent "checkDirectoryConflict" (runDirectoryConflictCheck -> searchStaffByEmail(directoryTerm)) where directoryTerm is attacker-controlled form input from any authenticated staff user. An attacker can inject filter logic (e.g. `*)(|(mail=*))(&(mail=` ) to broaden the search and enumerate directory entries.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: OS command injection (CWE-78): packageExportBundle() runs spawn('tar czf ' + archivePath + ' -C ' + workDir + ' export.csv --transform s|export.csv|' + reportType + '.csv|', [], { shell: true }). reportType is taken from the user-controlled form field 'reportType' (line 256, intent exportMattersBundle) and interpolated into a shell command string with shell:true and no quoting/validation (unlike packageRetentionExportBundle which uses the safe array form). A firm_admin can inject arbitrary shell commands through reportType, e.g. `$(touch /tmp/pwned)`. The tar output/exit is surfaced, and archivePath (also derived from reportType) is echoed back to the client in the success message, enabling command execution and exfiltration.

The response body is written to a document version in the current matter (lines 234-235), which the same authenticated user can then download, so an attacker can reach internal network services (metadata endpoints, localhost, cloud instance metadata) and retrieve their contents through the created version.

A crafted ?layout=<script>... payload executes in the victim's browser in the context of the authenticated documents session. extra.message: Use of hardcoded/default credential (CWE-798, CWE-1188): SESSION_SECRET falls back to the publicly-known default 'change-this-to-a-random-secret-in-production-min-32-chars-long' (also present in .env.example). The collab.server.ts chain also falls back through SESSION_SECRET to the same default.
